resolution: predict.edaphos_bhs() now returns the sampler's own predictive draws under draws = TRUE (as an attribute, so no existing caller changes), and data-raw/benchmark_wosis_p4_p5_p7.R uses them instead of rebuilding rnorm(200, mean, sd) from the summary. The cost of the substitution is measured rather than asserted: a paired diagnostic scores both distributions over the same predictions, fold and held-out truth, with the Gaussian drawn on a private RNG stream. On this archive it was CRPS 0.3405 vs 0.3420 and PICP90 0.9224 vs 0.9283 against a nominal 0.90; the per-fold table ships in the bundle as p7_gaussian_gap. The correction was propagated through benchmark_wosis_6pilar.rds, the README pooled table and the rendered manuscript.

data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R now writes inst/extdata/case_cerrado_results.rds directly, adopting the convention of the other 46 data-raw scripts, and carries an edaphos_provenance() block; the artefact was re-run and reproduced identical numbers, so the shipped file is now demonstrably the committed script's output rather than a hand copy from a gitignored path. tests/testthat/test-bundle-provenance.R -- which named this exact file as the defect it existed for and then skipped it -- now fails on any bundle without provenance outside an explicit legacy list that can only shrink. The header states plainly what a fresh clone needs: the two-script chain is public and reproducible but costs ~1 h and ~2 GB, and the 674 MB raster cannot be committed. Carrying the embeddings to remove that dependency was considered and rejected in writing: it would buy reproducibility of the output at the cost of making the E arm unfalsifiable.

The shipped artefact settles the contradiction: B1's 95% interval bounds are exactly 0.8 and 194.0, the exact min and max of soc_topsoil_gkg on the raw scale, so the target is untransformed g/kg with no log1p, over a surface-anchored slice of variable thickness (upper_depth == 0, lower_depth in 5-30 cm, median 15) rather than any fixed window. data-raw/case_cerrado_run.R's header claimed 'Target: log1p(SOC, g/kg). Point estimate = back-transformed MEDIAN' and defined a .back_transform that was never called; header, the kriging-scale sentence and the vignette's target line are corrected to the measured definition, and the dead function is gone.
